records.query: Need the auxiliary evidence texts covering detailed nail and skin examination findings, DIP joint imaging, and laboratory results including RF, anti-CCP, CRP/ESR, and microbial cultures, because confirming characteristic psoriatic nail changes and excluding infection or reactive arthritis is critical to validate the leading hypothesis.

Need the auxiliary evidence texts detailing personal or family history of psoriasis, specific nail morphology such as pitting, onycholysis or oil-drop sign, response to retinoids and methotrexate, and DIP joint imaging findings including erosions or proliferative changes, because these are the core items distinguishing psoriatic arthritis from reactive arthritis or infection.

records.query: Need detailed imaging of the hands/feet (X-ray or MRI) to assess DIP joint erosive changes, nail bed ultrasound or dermatology evaluation for psoriatic nail involvement, and laboratory tests including RF, anti-CCP, CRP/ESR, plus bacterial/fungal cultures to exclude infectious arthritis/osteomyelitis. These findings are core to confirm psoriatic arthritis and distinguish it from reactive or infectious alternatives.
records.text:
Laboratory tests: Screening assay for interferon-γ release for tuberculosis and hepatitis B and C were negative. Bacterial culture, complete blood cell count and coagulation tests had negative results.
Imaging studies:  Image Title: Hand radiography before treatment  Image Description: Bone erosions in the heads of phalanges in the middle and ring fingers on the left hand. No bone erosion in the fingers on the right hand.

records.query: Need additional laboratory and imaging data: RF, anti-CCP, CRP/ESR, fungal culture of nail pustules, and MRI of hands/feet to assess active inflammation and osteomyelitis; also dermatology confirmation of psoriatic nail changes. These are core to confirm psoriatic arthritis and exclude reactive/infectious causes.

bindings.label: Pustules beneath fingernails accompanied by redness and swelling of distal interphalangeal joints in both hands

Treatment history: initially treated with oral cefuroxime, followed by retinoids with topical corticosteroids, and oral methotrexate with topical corticosteroids; despite therapy, pustules and joint swelling worsened
Physical examination revealed 5 erythematous swollen and tender distal interphalangeal joints accompanied by pustules under dystrophic fingernails in both hands
Hand radiography reveals bone erosions in the left middle and ring finger phalangeal heads
TB and hepatitis serologies are negative
